title: Split a Message into Indexed Chunks
prompt:
Implement `split_indexed_message(message, limit) -> list[str]`. Split a message into the fewest nonempty consecutive payloads, then append an index suffix to every payload. If there are `n` chunks, the suffix for one-based chunk `i` is `#` followed by `i` padded with leading zeros to `max(2, len(str(n)))` digits. The suffix counts toward `limit` and every returned chunk must have length at most `limit`.

The payloads must preserve every character of `message`, including leading, trailing, and repeated whitespace: removing the suffix from each returned chunk and concatenating the payloads must reproduce `message` exactly. Return `[]` for an empty message. Raise `ValueError` when the inputs are invalid or `limit` cannot hold both one payload character and the shortest possible suffix.

This is a practice reconstruction of a reported Faire prompt. Its public examples disagree about whitespace at a chunk boundary, so this version deliberately uses an exact character-preservation contract.

example.reasoning: Each three-character payload leaves room for its three-character index suffix.
